concepts.mechanism_summary: Nalbinding creates fabric by passing the full length of a working thread through each loop using a single-eyed needle, unlike knitting where loops are formed without involving the free end. The technique involves 'driving yarn over/under/through loops wound around a thumb, thereby creating chains that stitched together make a multilayered, thick and cushy fabric that in most cases will not unravel.' Each loop is knotted in itself and also interlocked with adjacent loops.

atoms.mechanism_atom: Each new loop interlocks with previously created loops, producing a self-stabilising mesh that resists unravelling

concepts.mechanism_summary: In ikat, 'the resist is formed by binding individual yarns or bundles of yarns with a tight wrapping applied in the desired pattern' before dyeing. The bindings prevent dye penetration at wrapped segments: 'materials are tightly wrapped around sections of the yarn, compressing the fibers and preventing the dye from penetrating those areas.' After dyeing the bindings are removed and the yarns are woven, so the pattern is encoded in the yarn structure itself rather than applied to finished cloth.

atoms.mechanism_atom: Iterative rebinding and re-dyeing accumulates multiple color layers on the same yarn, composing complex multicolor patterns through sequential selective masking

atoms.verbatim_quote: in ikat the resist is applied to the yarns before they are woven into cloth. This fundamental difference means that both fabric faces are patterned in ikat
atoms.mechanism_atom: Pre-weave resist application separates pattern encoding (yarn-level) from fabric assembly, so pattern is intrinsic to yarn structure not surface-applied

concepts.mechanism_summary: Lost-wax casting works by encasing a wax positive model in refractory investment material, then burning out the wax to leave 'a hollow cavity in the shape of the original wax model.' Molten metal is forced into this negative cavity — via centrifugal, vacuum, or gravity pour — and after cooling the investment is broken away to reveal the metal duplicate. The burnout is critical: 'The burnout schedule is the single most critical variable in achieving clean castings.'

atoms.verbatim_quote: The heat causes the wax to melt and run out through the channels called sprues leaving behind a hollow cavity in the shape of the original wax model.
atoms.mechanism_atom: Thermal burnout transforms a solid wax positive into a hollow negative cavity that exactly encodes the original form

atoms.verbatim_quote: investment casting derives its name from the fact that the pattern is invested, or surrounded, with a refractory material
atoms.mechanism_atom: Encasing the sacrificial positive in investment material produces a rigid mold negative that survives the burnout and metal-pour stages

atoms.verbatim_quote: Once cooled, the flask is submerged in cold water to break up the investment and reveal the metal casting.
atoms.mechanism_atom: Post-pour quenching separates the investment shell from the solidified metal duplicate, completing the positive-negative-positive cycle

concepts.mechanism_summary: Kerf bending / lattice hinging works by making a staggered pattern of parallel through-cuts in a flat rigid sheet, dividing it into thin linked columns. 'The staggered pattern of cuts create thin elements that act as torsion springs within the material.' Each column 'can twist along its own length to let the sheet form a bend by twisting around the axis of these torsional links.' A curve is parameterized by spring length, spring width, and material thickness; the mechanism only works for developable (single-curvature) surfaces.

atoms.mechanism_atom: Distributed torsional compliance of cut columns transforms a locally rigid sheet into a globally flexible bending surface

concepts.mechanism_summary: Pattern welding forges two or more steels with differing carbon content into alternating layers by hammer-welding at high temperature. 'The Vikings, in particular, were fond of twisting bars of steel around each other, welding the bars together by hammering and then repeating the process with the resulting bars, to create complex patterns in the final steel bar.' Acid etching after polishing reveals the pattern because 'different steels react differently to acid, heat, and polishing' — the contrast between high- and low-carbon layers becomes visible as the flowing Damascus pattern.

atoms.mechanism_atom: Repeated fold-and-weld cycles accumulate hundreds of alternating high/low-carbon layers encoding structural heterogeneity into the steel billet

atoms.verbatim_quote: Different steels react differently to acid, heat, and polishing. When combined correctly, this contrast produces flowing lines, waves, ladders, raindrops, or mosaic-like designs.

concepts.mechanism_summary: Tensegrity is 'a structural principle based on a system of isolated components under compression inside a network of continuous tension, arranged so that the compressed members (usually bars or struts) do not touch each other.' Stability arises because as long as the angle between any two cables is smaller than 180 degrees the position of the rod is well defined. The structure achieves global rigidity through the interplay of pre-stressed tension cables and isolated compression struts — neither element type can achieve the structure alone.

atoms.verbatim_quote: a structural principle based on a system of isolated components under compression inside a network of continuous tension, arranged so that the compressed members (usually bars or struts) do not touch each other
atoms.mechanism_atom: Continuous tension network regulates the position and stability of isolated compression struts without any strut-to-strut contact

atoms.verbatim_quote: actuating one motor can change the entire shape of the robot, leading to complex, highly coupled dynamics
atoms.mechanism_atom: Load or actuation propagates through the tension network to globally reshape the entire structure, coupling local actuation to non-local deformation

atoms.verbatim_quote: Tensegrity robots are composed of rigid struts and flexible cables. These robots are lightweight, low cost, and capable of withstanding significant impacts by deforming and distributing force across the entire structure.
atoms.mechanism_atom: Impact force exchanges between rigid struts and flexible cables, distributing energy across the whole structure rather than concentrating it locally
